newsitem.title: USA: Three Georgia counties approve school GO bonds.
newsitem.headline: Three Georgia counties approve school GO bonds.

text.p: Three Georgia counties approved general obligation bonds for schools by narrow margins in Tuesday's elections, county officials said Wednesday.
In Spalding County, a $41.105 million school GO passed with 52.8 percent of the ballots cast. Bond proceeds will finance construction of three schools and renovation of 11 others.

In Houston County, voters approved a $34.5 million school bond issue by a similar close margin, with 52.5 percent of the votes cast. Bond proceeds will finance three new schools and expansions and renovations at 34 others. Debt service will be paid with a property tax increase that will raise the annual bill by about $20 for a $100,000 home.

In Meriwether County, voters approved a $15.06 million general obligation bond for schools, with about 56 percent of the votes cast. It was the county's first school bond referendum in 45 years, and one of its largest ever, Superintendent Robert Hawk said.
